narrative_markdown:
## Company overview

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a bank and financial holding company in the Financial Services sector, classified under Banks - Diversified. It operates across the United States, the rest of North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean. The business is organized into three segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management.

Its offerings include deposit, investment and lending products, cash management, mortgage origination and servicing, home equity loans, credit cards, payment solutions and auto loans. With a market capitalization of $883.53B, it is the largest company in its peer group shown here.

## Financial commentary

Revenue rose each year over the four fiscal years given, from $127.73B in 2022 to $154.95B in 2023, $169.44B in 2024 and $181.85B in 2025. Net income moved from $37.68B in 2022 to $49.55B in 2023 and $58.47B in 2024, then eased to $57.05B in 2025, so earnings dipped slightly even as revenue kept climbing.

The input reports a net margin of 34.9%, a return on equity of 17.8% and revenue growth of 30.4%. The dividend yield is 2.0%. The shares trade at $332.38, within a 52-week range of 279.10 to 366.50.

## Comps commentary

The primary multiple for this comparison is price-to-book. JPMorgan trades at 2.5 times book, which is 65% above the peer median of 1.5. Only Goldman Sachs at 2.5 and Morgan Stanley at 2.8 sit at similar levels among the peers.

On earnings, the trailing P/E of 14.2 is just 3% above the peer median of 13.8, while the forward P/E of 13.3 is 30% above the median of 10.2. The premium is supported by stronger fundamentals: return on equity is 41% above the median (17.8% against 12.6%) and revenue growth is 81% above it (30.4% against 16.8%). The dividend yield of 2.0% is 16% below the peer median of 2.4%, which fits a higher-valued stock. The analyst mean target in the data is 375.81, and the consensus label is "buy"; these are third-party views, not conclusions of this report.

## Risk commentary

The four most severe risks carry a severity of 3. They are heavy regulation and supervisory expectations, significant litigation and enforcement exposure, adverse economic and market conditions, and changes in interest rates and credit spreads. The last of these could affect earnings, liquidity and capital levels, and the macro risk could hurt results as well as investment and market-making positions.

Two risks carry a severity of 2: deterioration in the financial condition of clients, counterparties and central counterparties, and the sensitivity of the consumer businesses to economic conditions and government policies. The recent headlines concern institutional holdings, analyst price targets and a share price move of -3.34%. None relates directly to these filing risks.
